title: Titanium Seawater Strainer Housing
alloyReason: Grade 23 Ti-6Al-4V ELI (UNS R56401) is mandated for Titanium Seawater Strainer Housing where extra-low interstitial elements (O ≤0.13%, Fe ≤0.25%) provide superior fracture toughness (KIC >100 MPa√m) and fatigue crack growth resistance compared to standard Grade 5. The controlled oxygen content reduces susceptibility to strain-rate embrittlement, making it the preferred choice for Seawater strainer basket outer housing in safety-critical applications. This rationale is driven by seawater strainer basket outer housing and specific design requirements.
process: Ring forging radial-axial for marine piping geometry
CNC turn-bore operation with 0.5mm corner radius
TIG welding autogenous with 0.5mm corner radius
Hydrostatic pressure test with 0.5mm corner radius
surfaceTreatment: Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater — tailored for seawater strainer basket application
commonFailures: Crevice corrosion under biofouling in stagnant seawater - mitigated by CP-Ti Grade 2 + ICCP system — critical for seawater strainer basket performance

faq.q: What is the seawater corrosion rate of Titanium Seawater Strainer Housing?
faq.a: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V exhibits a general corrosion rate of <0.01 mm/year in quiescent seawater and <0.05 mm/year in high-flow (5 m/s) seawater. Unlike stainless steels, Titanium Seawater Strainer Housing is immune to chloride stress corrosion cracking and pitting corrosion up to 260°C. For seawater strainer basket in submerged service, no cathodic protection is required — a significant cost advantage over steel and aluminum.

Sample evaluation (1-5 units) can be expedited to 5-7 business days. Volume pricing is available for production quantities above 100 units.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Seawater Strainer Housing?
faq.a: Each Titanium Seawater Strainer Housing shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for seawater strainer basket.
